name: Sphinx, Canisphinx
body:
Canisphinx
CR 5

This chimeric beast has the body of a tawny lion but the head and neck of a shaggy-haired jackal, with wide wings that are more bat-like than bird.

XP 1,600
NE Large magical beast
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 10, flat-footed 17 (+1 Dex, +8 natural, –1 size)
hp 57 (6d10+24)
Fort +9, Ref +6, Will +7

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 80 ft. (poor)
Melee bite +10 (2d8+7 plus grab)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks rake (2 claws +10, 2d6+5), roar

STATISTICS

Str 21, Dex 13, Con 18, Int 15, Wis 16, Cha 14
Base Atk +6; CMB +12 (+16 grapple); CMD 23 (27 vs. trip)
Feats Flyby Attack, Iron Will, Vital Strike
Skills Fly +2, Intimidate +8, Knowledge (any one) +6, Perception +10, Survival +9
Languages Common, Sphinx

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Roar (Su)

A canisphinx can roar up to three times per day as a standard action. Each progressive roar has a different effect, depending upon whether it is the first, second, or third of the canisphinx’s roars for that day. All of these roars are sonic effects that fill a 60-foot burst, centered on the canisphinx; the save DCs are Charisma-based. Sphinxes are immune to all of the effects of a canisphinx’s roars.

First Roar: Affected creatures become frightened for 2d4 rounds (DC 15 Will negates). This is a mind-affecting fear effect in addition to being a sonic effect.

Second Roar: Affected creatures are paralyzed with fear for 1d4 rounds (DC 15 Will negates). This is a mind-affecting fear effect in addition to being a sonic effect.

Third Roar: Affected creatures take 2d6 points of sonic damage and are paralyzed and deafened for 2d6 rounds. A DC 15 Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the paralyzed and deafened conditions.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts, hills, or plains
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Among the cruelest and least intelligent of sphinxes, canisphinxes have heads resembling jackals, with black-brown fur fading to gray on their underside and a coat of tawny fur edged with black. They are ardent hunters, enjoying long chases across the savannahs and desert sands either afoot or in the air. They are endurance hunters, dogging the trail of their prey until it literally collapses from exhaustion. Canisphinxes tend to be solitary, though mated pairs may hunt together, and occasionally small packs will form, typically along family lines. These packs rarely stay together long, however, as they rapidly devolve into internecine squabbling over the spoils of prey and end up with the most dominant canisphinx driving its weaker rivals away or killing them. Canisphinxes are not terribly brave, preferring to select prey that is already weak, injured, or otherwise vulnerable, driving it away from allies and support before pinning it down and finishing it off.
